name: imbl
summary: The maintained fork of Rust’s `im` crate: persistent collections with an RRB-tree `Vector`, a hash array mapped trie `HashMap` and a B+ tree `OrdMap`, with O(1) cloning and copy-on-write updates.
intro: `imbl` continues the `im` crate after its author stopped maintaining it. Its 1.0 release was fully compatible with `im` 15.0.0, so switching is mostly a change of crate name. It offers the same immutable versions of the standard collections: `Vector` (an RRB tree with O(log n) split and concatenation), `HashMap` and `HashSet` (hash array mapped tries) and `OrdMap` and `OrdSet` (B+ trees since version 6.0.0). Each tree node holds up to 64 values.

Cloning only bumps a reference count, and a node is copied only when a shared clone changes it; a node nobody else shares is updated in place, about an order of magnitude faster than an immutable update. Collections use thread-safe `Arc` by default. Instead of a separate `im-rc` crate, `imbl` makes the pointer type a parameter through the `archery` crate, so single-threaded code can use `GenericVector<T, RcK>` with `Rc`, and a `triomphe` feature swaps in a faster `Arc`. Like `im`, it is slower than the standard collections at their best operations: `Vec` wins below several hundred elements and `OrdMap` runs 2 to 3 times slower than `BTreeMap`.

The fork has kept releasing: it fixed critical `Vector` bugs in 2.0.0 (2022), rewrote `OrdMap` as a B+ tree in 6.0.0 (July 2025), sped up `HashMap` and the B-tree in 7.0.0 (January 2026), and shipped 7.0.2 in September 2026. It needs Rust 1.85 or later.
strengths: A drop-in path off the archived `im` crate, with bug fixes in `Vector`, `OrdMap` and `OrdSet`
O(1) `clone`, structural sharing and in-place updates of unshared nodes
`Vector` concatenates, splits and inserts in the middle in O(log n), which `Vec` and `VecDeque` can’t
The shared pointer type is pluggable: `Arc` by default, `Rc` for single-threaded code, or `triomphe::Arc`
limits: Slower than `Vec` for small collections and than `BTreeMap` for ordered maps, as with `im`
Values must be `Clone`; expensive values need wrapping in `Rc` or `Arc`
Frequent major versions (2.0 in 2022, then 3.0 to 7.0 between 2024 and 2026), and a minimum Rust version that rises over time

story: Bodil Stokke’s `im` crate (2017) brought RRB vectors, hash array mapped tries and B-tree maps to Rust, but its last release, 15.1.0, came out in April 2022 and the repository was later archived.

Joe Neeman forked it as `imbl` in August 2021 and released 1.0.0 on 11 August, “our fork/continuation of `im`”, fully compatible with `im` 15.0.0 apart from fixes to deleting from and iterating over large ordered maps and sets. Later releases fixed critical `Vector` bugs (2.0.0, 2022), made the pointer type generic so one crate covers both `Arc` and `Rc` (5.0.0, 2025), rewrote `OrdMap` and `OrdSet` as B+ trees (6.0.0, 2025) and improved `HashMap` memory use and speed (6.1.0 and 7.0.0).

choices.why: Users of the unmaintained `im` crate could switch by changing a dependency, so 1.0 matched `im` 15.0.0 and listed only the fixes made since.

choices.choice: One crate with a generic pointer type
choices.why: Instead of publishing twin crates like `im` and `im-rc`, the `archery` crate lets each collection take `Arc`, `Rc` or `triomphe::Arc` as a type parameter.
Version 6.0.0 rewrote `OrdMap` and `OrdSet` as B+ trees for significant performance gains, keeping O(log n) operations.

timeline.text: 5.0.0 adds pluggable pointer types; 6.0.0 rewrites `OrdMap` as a B+ tree
7.0.0 (January) speeds up `HashMap` and the B-tree; 7.0.2 in September
